stages.title: Meet your radio
stages.need: The parts list and a clear workbench.
stages.action: Understand the three controls and the order of the build.
stages.expect: You can explain how a tag selects audio and how the battery switch works.
checks: I have a computer, internet and a phone that can write NFC tags.
I understand that soldering and adult assembly are required.

stages.title: Gather your parts
stages.need: The shopping list, supplier pages and tools.
stages.action: Match the product codes and check the accessories before ordering.
stages.expect: Every required part and tool is accounted for.
checks: I have checked the exact board, display, reader and battery product codes.
I have allowed for wires, headers, tools, mounting hardware and delivery.

stages.title: Get to know the pins
stages.need: Unpowered boards, soldering tools, light and magnifier.
stages.action: Identify the labelled pins and solder the loose headers.
stages.expect: Headers are secure, with no solder bridging neighbouring pads.
checks: USB and battery are disconnected.
I can distinguish VCC, 3V3, GND and the speaker outputs.
I have inspected the solder joints.

stages.title: Give the board its first program
stages.need: Bare DFR1139, computer and USB data cable.
stages.action: Install the pinned software, download Hardware test, then Verify and Upload.
stages.expect: Serial Monitor at 115200 reports PSRAM: OK (2097152 bytes).
checks: The exact core, library versions and Tools settings are selected.
The complete extracted sketch verifies and uploads.
The bare board reports PSRAM: OK (2097152 bytes).

stages.title: Bring the controls to life
stages.need: OLED, pot, button, RC522, short jumpers and breadboard.
stages.action: Connect and test the screen first, then controls, then the reader.
stages.expect: The screen works, the knob reaches mute/cap, and each button press counts once.
checks: The OLED works in Hardware test.
The knob reaches zero and the cap; one press gives one button count.
The RC522 reports a version other than 00 or FF.

stages.title: Connect the sound
stages.need: Amplifier, speaker, 22 AWG leads and multimeter.
stages.action: Measure the two supply rails, unplug power, then connect the amplifier.
stages.expect: 3V3 is about 3.3 V; VCC is about 4.5–5.0 V on USB. Speaker leads are isolated from GND.
checks: I measured the power rails with the meter in DC-voltage mode.
The amplifier uses VCC and its GAIN pin is linked to VIN.
Only the speaker leads connect to the amplifier speaker terminals.

stages.title: Your first station
stages.need: Home 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi details and the assembled USB bench circuit.
stages.action: Generate Normal radio firmware, upload, and raise the knob gently.
stages.expect: You hear a station, can mute it, and can change stations with one press.
checks: The radio joins Wi-Fi and plays the chosen stations.
Mute and station changes work.
Playback recovers after an internet interruption.

stages.title: Give a story a home
stages.need: Writable NTAG213/215, NFC-writing phone and a public audio URL.
stages.action: Write one URL record, read it back, then present the card to the reader.
stages.expect: Audio starts; the station button returns to radio.
checks: The phone reads back the complete URL as a URL/URI record.
The short test file plays on the actual radio.
I tried the story card, removing and presenting it again to replay.

stages.title: Find a comfortable level
stages.need: Finished USB circuit and your intended listening position.
stages.action: Start at minimum, test representative audio, and reduce the cap if needed.
stages.expect: Listening is quiet and clear; a software step is never treated as a sound-level measurement.
checks: I checked listening level away from ears.
I know to repeat this check with a full battery and the finished enclosure.

stages.title: Make it portable
stages.need: Protected pack, separate extension, switch, soldering tools and meter.
stages.action: Build and measure the disconnected extension harness, then test all four power states.
stages.expect: Battery playback and charging behave as shown in the table.
checks: I checked extension continuity and battery connector polarity.
All four USB/switch states behave as documented.
Current, temperature and supply stability have been checked under load.

stages.title: Make it yours
stages.need: Bench-tested radio, actual enclosure, ruler and cardboard.
stages.action: Make a full-size layout, verify clearances, then mount and repeat the checks.
stages.expect: Controls, audio, NFC and charging work with the lid closed.
checks: The actual parts fit with space for connectors, wires and access.
The closed lid passes NFC, reception and playback checks.
Battery, wiring and all small parts are secure.

stages.title: Find a fix
stages.need: The symptom you see and Serial Monitor if available.
stages.action: Choose a symptom and work through one check at a time.
stages.expect: You have a working checkpoint or useful observations to ask for help.
checks: I have recorded unresolved symptoms and useful diagnostic messages.

stages.title: Keep it working
stages.need: Your private configured sketch and build notes.
stages.action: Keep configuration private and use the maintenance notes for updates.
stages.expect: You can reproduce the build and know what still needs physical verification.
checks: My configured sketch is stored privately.
I have kept the part details, settings and measurements for this radio.

tools: Soldering iron, stand, electronics solder and flux
Side cutters, wire strippers and small screwdrivers
Multimeter with DC volts, resistance and continuity
Ruler, drill and file or small saw
Eye protection and a ventilated work area
Computer with Arduino IDE support and USB data cable
Internet access and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi details
Phone capable of writing NFC tags
Cardboard, paper, pencil and masking tape for a trial layout

glossary.GPIO: A numbered input or output on the ESP32. Match the GPIO number and board label, not the hole position.
glossary.3V3: The regulated 3.3-volt supply for the screen, reader and potentiometer.
glossary.VCC: This board’s USB/battery supply output. It powers the amplifier and is different from 3V3.
glossary.GND: The circuit’s shared electrical reference. Neither speaker output belongs on this rail.
glossary.I2C: A two-signal link (SDA and SCL) used by the OLED screen.
glossary.I2S: The digital audio link from the ESP32 to the amplifier. It uses BCLK, LRC and DIN.
glossary.SPI: The signal interface used by the RC522. Its SDA-labelled pin acts as chip select here.
glossary.PSRAM: Extra working memory used by the audio library. The selected board has 2 MB.
glossary.Sketch: The Arduino project folder: one .ino file plus all of its .h files.
glossary.Compile / Verify: Translate the sketch into a program and check it for build errors.
glossary.Upload: Copy the compiled program from your computer to the ESP32 over USB.
glossary.Serial Monitor: Arduino IDE’s text window for messages from the board. Set its baud rate to 115200.
glossary.Continuity: A meter test for a connected electrical path. Use it only with the circuit unpowered.
glossary.NDEF URI: The URL record stored on a story card. The audio stays online, not on the card.
